samples.summary: New copy-time refusal (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap` → BadRequestException) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `document-copy.service.ts:446` adds a user-visible 400 on copying a document containing a table at the nesting cap. `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts` has ~40 cases (grep for `describe(|it(`) and none mentions nesting; grep for `nested|NestingCap` in that spec returns no matches. Nothing anywhere else in packages/backend references `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` from a test. So neither the refusal nor its complement (an ordinary deep-but-legal document still copying) is pinned — if the predicate over-fires, every copy of a normal document breaks; if it under-fires, the copy silently drops rows, which is the exact data loss the hunk claims to prevent.

samples.summary: The tightened request-body depth check (`> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` → `>= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) is not distinguished by any test
samples.evidence: `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (docs-content.controller.ts:817) and `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32`, so the change moves the accepted ceiling by exactly one level. The only depth tests are in `docs-content.validation.spec.ts:82-113`, which use `OVERFLOW_DEPTH = 20000` (rejected) and depth `2` (accepted) — both pass identically before and after the hunk. No test exercises depth 31 (must be accepted) or 32 (must now be 400), i.e. the boundary this hunk exists to move, and whose failure mode per the hunk's own comment is a body that validates and then 500s in `writeDocsRoot` or writes a table the editor truncates.

samples.summary: New silent decline in `setHeader`/`setFooter` (replacesTruncatedRows gate) is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds decline-and-return guards to `setHeader` and `setFooter` in yorkie-doc-store.ts. The new suite in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` ("the write side carries the read side's nesting cap") covers only `setDocument`, `insertBlockAfter`, `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `insertTableRow`, `insertTableColumn`. Grep for `setHeader|setFooter` in that test file returns only three pre-existing calls at lines 2017/2033/2047, none about nesting. A wrong gate here silently swallows a header/footer edit with only a console.warn.
searchedFor: read the new nesting-cap describe block in that test file

samples.summary: `blockPathNestingDepth` is only exercised for the body region; the header/footer prefix length (2) is untested
samples.evidence: The helper branches on `region === 'body' ? 1 : 2`. Every new incremental-writer test in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts builds its chain with `store.setDocument({ blocks: [...] })` and uses `cellPath()` starting `[0]` — a body path. No test writes incrementally into a table nested inside a header or footer, so an off-by-one in the header/footer prefix (which would restart the cap counter one level off for every header edit) cannot be caught.
searchedFor: grep setHeader/setFooter in that test file

samples.summary: The paste call sites' depth arithmetic (`doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId)`, and `+ (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` in `pasteTableCells`) has no test
samples.evidence: `capTableNesting`/`capTableCellsNesting` are unit-tested in packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts, but always with a hand-supplied `baseDepth`. No test drives a paste through `insertBlocks`/`pasteTableCells` to check the depth actually computed at the call site. An error there either silently drops a pasted nested table (visible content loss) or lets a paste write past the cap, which the CRDT writer then refuses.

samples.summary: The editor-level `insertTable` refusal at the nesting cap (silent `return`) is untested
samples.evidence: editor.ts now returns early when `doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`. Tests cover only the model backstop (`packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:156` — `doc.insertTableInCell(...)` throws). No test asserts the command declines cleanly (in particular, that no stray empty paragraph is left behind, which the comment says is the whole reason the check precedes the split).

samples.summary: `buildCellRangeRects`' new clamp to the resolved layout table is untested

The new clamp test in packages/docs/test/view/nested-table-cell-range.test.ts ('clamps a peer-written cell rectangle to the table it names') exercises normalizeCellRange, which clamps first — so the buildCellRangeRects fallback is never reached by any test.

samples.summary: The spread→reduce change in `visitCellRectangleSlices` (RangeError avoidance for >~100k rows) has no test
samples.evidence: The hunk replaces `Math.max(0, ...rows.map(...))` with a fold specifically so a peer-sized row count does not throw RangeError. No test in packages/docs/test constructs a table with a row count large enough to trigger the old spread limit, so the regression it fixes is not pinned. (The analogous fold in selection.ts's normalizeCellRange is likewise untested at scale.)
searchedFor: reviewed new tests in table-nesting.test.ts and cell-range-expand.test.ts

samples.summary: Filler assertions in the Shift+Tab cycle test (`expect(leafId).toBeDefined()`, `typeof blockId === 'string'`) hold regardless of the guard
samples.evidence: In 'Shift+Tab out of the last cell stops instead of overflowing', only `expect(press(container,'Tab',true)).toBeUndefined()` can fail if the cycle guard is removed; `expect(typeof editor._getCursorForTest().blockId).toBe('string')` and `expect(leafId).toBeDefined()` are true for any outcome. They read as coverage but add none. (The companion ArrowRight test, which counts getBlock lookups, is a real assertion.)

samples.summary: Backend writer boundary tested one level low: accepted case uses MAX-1 tables, not the deepest legal chain
samples.evidence: `nested(depth)` builds `depth` tables with the innermost at depth `depth-1`. The accepting test uses `nested(MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH - 1)` (innermost at MAX-2) and the refusing one `nested(MAX+1)` (innermost at MAX), so the exact legal ceiling — `nested(MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)`, innermost at MAX-1, which `writeDocsRoot` must accept — is never written. The frontend suite does pin this boundary (`nestedTableBlock(MAX)` not throwing); the backend one leaves a one-level hole where an over-strict writer would go unnoticed.
searchedFor: compared with frontend yorkie-doc-store.test.ts boundary cases

finding.summary: New copy-time refusal (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap` → BadRequestException) has no test at all
finding.evidence: `document-copy.service.ts:446` adds a user-visible 400 on copying a document containing a table at the nesting cap. `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts` has ~40 cases (grep for `describe(|it(`) and none mentions nesting; grep for `nested|NestingCap` in that spec returns no matches. Nothing anywhere else in packages/backend references `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` from a test. verdict.reason: The refusal exists at document-copy.service.ts:446-451 (BadRequestException 'Cannot copy this document: it contains a table nested too deeply to be read completely') in the 'doc' arm of copyContent. No test anywhere exercises it: repo-wide greps for the message string, for documentHasTableAtNestingCap, and for MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH within packages/backend return no test hits on the copy path; all ~40 it()/describe() titles in document-copy.service.spec.ts were enumerated and none covers nesting (its BadRequestException assertions at lines 412/449/578/637/697 cover blob-id validation, unknown type, and the image fail policy); packages/backend/test/document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts contains no 'table' occurrence at all. The closest coverage, docs-tree.spec.ts:711-757, pins the predicate's edges only through writeDocsRoot (accepts cap-1, throws /nested at or past/ at cap, header too) — that mitigates the 'over-fires' half of the risk but is a different function in a different module; deleting the copy-service branch would leave every test green, so the 400 (versus a generic writer throw after re-hosting work) is unpinned. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed, user-visible behavior with no meaningful test.

finding.summary: The tightened request-body depth check (`> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` → `>= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) is not distinguished by any test
finding.evidence: `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (docs-content.controller.ts:817) and `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32`, so the change moves the accepted ceiling by exactly one level. The only depth tests are in `docs-content.validation.spec.ts:82-113`, which use `OVERFLOW_DEPTH = 20000` (rejected) and depth `2` (accepted) — both pass identically before and after the hunk. No test exercises depth 31 (must be accepted) or 32 (must now be 400), i.e. the boundary this hunk exists to move, and whose failure mode per the hunk's own comment is a body that validates and then 500s in `writeDocsRoot` or writes a table the editor truncates.

verdict.reason: The tightened check is real and untested at its boundary. docs-content.controller.ts:454 rejects at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (32, packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26) while the sibling walks still use `> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (=32, :817, used at :851 and :1191), so the accepted ceiling moved by exactly one level, as the hunk's own comment at :446-453 states. The only tests over this walk are docs-content.validation.spec.ts:82-113: rejection at OVERFLOW_DEPTH=20000 and acceptance at depth 2 — both outcomes identical under `>32` and `>=32`, so neither can fail if the boundary regresses. I searched wider than the reviewer: repo-wide grep for `nested too deeply` (only those two specs plus the element-walk test at docs-content.controller.spec.ts:1675-1690, which nests 200 `group` elements through `data.children`, a different counter), repo-wide grep for MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (the only backend test hit is docs-tree.spec.ts:711-757, which asserts writeDocsRoot's own `/nested at or past/` throw, not the controller's BadRequestException), grep for nestedTableBlocks across packages/backend (only depths 20000 and 2), and the other callers of assertValidDocsBody (template/seed/catalog.spec.ts:72-76, shallow seed content). No test exercises depth 31 (must be accepted) or 32 (must now be 400), so a regression of this guard ships undetected as either a 500/truncated table or a wrongly-rejected legitimate body.
